items.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
items.summary_1line: Proposes PreVIR, a lightweight text-only router that decides from the source sentence alone whether to invoke visual features in English-to-Chinese machine translation, reducing visual calls while keeping quality near always-on multimodal inference.
items.editor_note: 텍스트 전용 라우터가 번역에 이미지가 필요한 시점을 판단해 시각 호출을 줄인다.

items.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
items.summary_1line: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. Recent industria...
items.editor_note: 온톨로지를 구축하는 에이전트를 위한 과제 기반 벤치마크.

items.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
items.summary_1line: Search-RSI is a self-improvement framework for multimodal search agents that expands the retrieval world with new tasks and evidence, reporting 9.8 and 9.5 point average accuracy gains at 9B and 27B across nine benchmarks.
items.editor_note: Search-RSI 자기 개선은 9B와 27B에서 각각 9.8점, 9.5점의 향상을 보고했다.

items.title: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Evaluates zero-shot multilingual aspect-based sentiment triplet extraction across 12 languages, three domains and seven open-weight LLMs under four prompting strategies, finding direct monolithic prompting performs best.
items.editor_note: 12개 언어와 7개 오픈 웨이트 모델을 대상으로 한 실험에서, 감성 트리플렛 추출은 정교한 전략보다 직접적인 단일 프롬프트가 더 나았다.

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary_1line: Describes a two-tier industrial framework for automated UX attribution in web search: a fine-tuned Gemini XS telemetry model for macro sentiment regression detection, and a Gemini 3.0 Pro multimodal model for layout-level diagnostics.
items.editor_note: 검색 UX 감성 하락의 원인을 분석하는 2단계 Gemini 파이프라인.

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: MemOnce proposes an LLM architecture that caches compact final-layer hidden states as memory and decodes them into KV caches, reporting a 1313× smaller memory state cache and 6.9× lower prefill latency for Qwen3.5-4B at 1M context.
items.editor_note: MemOnce는 컨텍스트 1M의 Qwen3.5-4B에서 메모리 캐시가 1313배 작아지고 프리필 레이턴시가 6.9배 낮아졌다고 보고했다.

items.title: Population-Based Post-Training for Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Introduces Population-Based Post-Training (PBPT), which trains several RLVR models in parallel and uses population-based training to tune hyperparameters, reporting stronger agents than compute-matched independent runs on four benchmarks.
items.editor_note: 집단 기반 학습으로 병렬 실행 전반에서 RLVR 하이퍼파라미터를 튜닝한다.

items.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware
items.summary_1line: KernelShift is a benchmark that tests coding agents on CPU kernel optimization across Arm Neon, SVE, SVE2 and SME2, finding agents beat the compiler and some libraries but lag KleidiAI and struggle with SME2.
items.editor_note: KernelShift: 코딩 에이전트가 Arm 커널에서 컴파일러를 앞섰지만 KleidiAI에는 못 미치고 SME2에서 어려움을 겪었다.

items.title: Training-Free Interventions for Hallucination in Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: A survey of 116 works on inference-time methods for reducing LLM hallucination, comparing intervention families by evidence source, model access, and preparation cost, and noting metrics and limits to reported gains.
items.editor_note: 학습이 필요 없는 환각 해결책 116가지를 필요 접근 권한과 준비 비용을 기준으로 비교한 서베이.

items.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
items.summary_1line: Presents mini-psych-agent, which converts psychological tasks into interactive environments and uses a learned human-policy model to measure how closely LLM agents' behavior matches human choices, finding this varies with agent configuration and task.
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agentic, harness, evaluation.
items.editor_note: 심리학 과제 환경에서 에이전트의 선택이 얼마나 인간과 유사한지 측정한다.

items.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Introduces CONCOR, a controlled benchmark that scores how contrastive decoding methods rank ground-truth objects against hallucinated candidates in multimodal LLMs, using a Contrastive Grounding Margin metric.
items.editor_note: CONCOR는 대조 디코딩이 실제 객체와 환각 객체의 순위를 어떻게 매기는지를 기준으로 점수를 다시 매긴다.

items.title: Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Proposes Lobals, a training-free decoding method that re-runs a contiguous window of MLLM layers with the strongest visual-token attention to revisit visual evidence, reporting gains on vision-language, hallucination, and vision-centric tasks.
items.editor_note: Lobals는 학습 없이 디코딩 시점에 시각적 주의가 가장 높은 레이어를 다시 실행한다.

items.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: LatentParse is a training-free framework that uses an analyst VLM to parse CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features into a text report of spatial evidence, improving five VLMs by 0.7-2.4 points on three spatial benchmarks.
items.editor_note: 분석가 VLM이 비전 인코더 특징을 텍스트 공간 보고서로 변환해 0.7~2.4점을 더한다.

items.title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
items.summary_1line: Introduces InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark that labels six fine-grained information manipulation strategies in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, and fabrication, plus a coarse consistency label, and benchmarks representative multimodal models on it.
items.editor_note: InfoCon은 멀티모달 대화에서 정보 은폐, 조작 등 여섯 가지 정보 조작 전략에 레이블을 붙인다.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary_1line: Introduces ToolSmith, a framework that automatically generates and reuses new tools on top of a lean base library for multimodal search agents, evaluated on 13 benchmarks with gains that grow with backbone size.
items.editor_note: ToolSmith는 멀티모달 검색 에이전트를 위한 도구를 생성하고 재사용하며, 백본이 클수록 성능 향상 폭이 커진다.

items.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Proposes ReQOR, a training-free defense against quantization-conditioned backdoors in LLMs that repairs dominant same-state operator discrepancies on benign calibration data via a factorized residual adapter, tested on four LLMs.
items.editor_note: ReQOR: 양자화 이후에만 발동하는 백도어를 학습 없이 복구한다.

items.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
items.summary_1line: LEGOSpec is a modular framework that splits speculative decoding draft models into four swappable components and trains them under matched conditions, yielding the DFlux draft that improves acceptance length on Qwen and Gemma models.
items.editor_note: 추측 디코딩 연재에서 이어지는 항목: LEGOSpec은 교체 가능한 드래프트 구성요소를 학습하며, DFlux 드래프트는 수락 길이를 늘린다.

items.title: Joint Estimation of Abilities and Item Parameters for Large Language Models Using Probability and Binary Responses: A Fractional-Response IRT Framework
items.summary_1line: Large language model (LLM) evaluations provide two response types: probabilities assigned to correct answers and binary indicators of correctness. Restricting evaluation to one type narrows the range of available models or discards probability information. We propose a method to
items.editor_note: 답변 확률과 이진 정답 여부를 모두 사용해 모델을 채점하는 IRT 프레임워크.

items.title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
items.summary_1line: Introduces Merlin-Bench, a benchmark of 100 cases across 15 problem families that tests whether LLM agents can produce proofs a formal verifier accepts under interactive-proof protocols, and reports that 10 frontier LLMs struggle with this.
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, eval.
items.editor_note: Merlin-Bench: 최첨단 LLM 10종이 형식 검증기가 받아들이는 증명을 만드는 데 어려움을 겪는다.

items.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary_1line: Proposes EVA, a visual agent that reduces multimodal LLM hallucinations by gathering external visual evidence through iterative tool replanning, verifying answers against that evidence, and invoking tools selectively.
items.editor_note: EVA는 외부 시각 증거를 가져와 이를 바탕으로 답을 검증하며, 도구를 선택적으로 호출한다.

items.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
items.summary_1line: Data management systems organize large text collections for tasks such as finding relevant studies and extracting contract clauses. Systems make long documents searchable by splitting them into independently indexed c...
items.editor_note: ConTra는 독립적으로 인덱싱된 청크가 문서 컨텍스트를 유지하도록 프리픽스 생성을 학습시킨다.

items.title: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding
items.summary_1line: Introduces PoVi, a benchmark and agentic framework that turns poems into narrated videos via knowledge-grounded planning, reporting gains over single-call generation across three planners and four video generators.
items.editor_note: PoVi: 시를 영상으로 만드는 작업에서는 에이전트 기반 계획이 단일 호출 생성보다 낫다.

items.title: Show HN: Dev-Mem – Local-first SQLite knowledge graph for AI coding agents
items.summary_1line: Dev-Mem is a local-first tool that gives AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode a persistent SQLite knowledge store of decisions, failed approaches and constraints, injected into new sessions and optionally shared via Git.
items.editor_note: 가장 최근 항목: Dev-Mem은 코딩 에이전트에 결정 사항과 실패한 접근법을 담은 로컬 SQLite 저장소를 제공하며, 원하면 Git으로 공유할 수 있다.

editorial.tldr: This thread was regrouped from a speculative-decoding run into a broad bucket of 77 papers and posts sharing the phrase "large language", mostly arXiv, from Nov 6. Its largest strands are hallucination fixes, which moved from preference alignment to decode-time methods, eval-validity papers, and RAG and agent-memory designs.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 26: Dev-Mem, a Show HN tool, gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode a local SQLite store of past decisions and failed approaches, a day after Merlin-Bench found 10 frontier LLMs struggle to produce verifier-accepted proofs.
editorial.why_it_matters: The useful signal for platform teams is in two strands: RAG citations can misstate provenance undetected, and eval scores move with rater drift and prompt framing, so both retrieval attribution and regression evals need their own checks.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before trusting RAG citations, sample answers and check that the cited passage actually supports the claim; when a regression eval moves, re-score an older baseline with today's judges or rubric first to rule out rater drift.

beats.headline: RAG and agent memory: compress, compact, or build a knowledge graph
beats.summary: From pixel-compressed context to compacted fact memory, plus evidence that RAG citations misstate their sources.

beats.headline: Eval papers question what benchmark scores measure
beats.summary: Rater drift, framing effects, adaptive users and hidden recall all move scores without the model changing.

Hallucination work shifts to training-free, decode-time fixes
beats.summary: Mid-month preference-alignment papers give way to a 116-paper survey of inference-time methods and a benchmark that re-scores contrastive decoding.

LLMs writing kernels and planning training infrastructure
beats.summary: Kernel benchmarks on CUDA, Ascend and Arm, plus the one speculative-decoding paper left from this thread's earlier arc.

beats.headline: Attacks on AI infrastructure and model-level defenses
Applied agents and tool use, grouped in by wording
Verifiable outputs and persistent memory for coding agents
beats.summary: Nov 25-26: a formal-proof benchmark, evidence-checking visual agents, context-preserving chunk retrieval, and Dev-Mem.

open_questions: Does any decode-time hallucination fix from the Nov 23 survey ship in a mainstream serving engine such as vLLM or SGLang?
Do MemOnce's 1313x memory-cache and 6.9x prefill-latency figures for Qwen3.5-4B at 1M context reproduce outside the authors' setup?
Does a citation-provenance check of the kind in "Cited but Unused" appear in an open RAG evaluation toolkit?
Does persistent agent memory like Dev-Mem get a measured effect on coding-agent task success, not just a demo?
